chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Qutaybah al-A'sha said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was in his presence, and a man said to him, 'My brother goes to the mountain to bring sheep, so he gives an advance payment (salam) for the sheep, specifying known ages, for a known term, so he is given a four-year-old in place of a two-year-old.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Is it by the goodwill/agreement of his companion (the seller)?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.يَسْلُمُ: To give an advance payment (Salam contract)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Salam contract regarding the delivery of livestock of varying ages?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of the Salam contract (bay' al-salam) in Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the permissibility of delivering livestock of a different age or quality within agreed parameters. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that such flexibility is valid provided the transaction is conducted with mutual consent and goodwill (bi-tibbati nafsin), reflecting the principle of contractual freedom in commercial dealings. This ruling underscores the practical application of Salam in agrarian societies, ensuring liquidity for farmers while protecting buyers from ambiguity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Quteyba Al A’asha who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My brother stays behind at the mountain milking the sheep, so he submits an advance payment regarding the sheep of known years, to a known term. So he is given the four year old in place of the five year old’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Is it by the agreement of his companion himself?’ So he said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Qutaybah al-’A‘sha’ who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was present, by a man who said, ‘My brother comes from and goes to the mountains, milks sheep of known age for an appointed time; then he is given four years old in place of three years old.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is it with fine consent of his party?’ he replied, ‘Yes, it is so.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
